title: Stock of the week: United Parcel Service
summary: United Parcel Service (UPS) recently experienced significant stock gains following a strong second-quarter 2019 earnings report, driven by better-than-expected performance and increased sales and profits. The company's ongoing transformation process, focusing on automation and increased sorting/shipping capacity, is showing positive results, helping to improve margins and mitigate risks from a slowing global economy. Despite being a cyclical business susceptible to trade issues, UPS's dividend yield and strategic investments in e-commerce infrastructure position it well for future growth.

title: Kroger Is Upping Its Advertising Game
summary: Kroger, the nation's second-largest food retailer, has hired global advertising agency DDB as its creative "agency of record" to burnish its brand identity and enhance its consumer-experience focus. This move aims to drive more customers to choose Kroger across its stores and online, especially as part of its "Restock Kroger" initiative, which focuses on technology and omnichannel experiences. The company is investing in digital sales, aiming for $9 billion in annual returns, and exploring innovations like driverless car deliveries, while facing challenges with its diverse brand portfolio and the cost-effectiveness of online grocery shopping.

title: Could Amazon Lose the Pentagon JEDI Project?
summary: The Pentagon's new Secretary of Defense Mike Esper announced a review of the bidding process for the $10 billion JEDI cloud computing contract, raising concerns for Amazon. This review follows protests from Oracle and IBM, as well as doubts expressed by President Trump about the competitive bidding process. The news caused Amazon's stock to slide, highlighting the significance of the contract and the political scrutiny surrounding it.

title: IBM fired as many as 1,00,000 employees in recent years to make itself look 'cool' and 'trendy', finds lawsuit
summary: IBM has reportedly fired as many as 100,000 employees in recent years to appear "cool" and "trendy" to millennials, according to a former vice president's deposition in an age discrimination lawsuit. The company, facing multiple lawsuits, aimed to shed its "old fuddy-duddy organization" image to better compete with companies like Amazon and Google. This strategy involved deliberately targeting older workers through rolling layoffs to "correct its seniority mix."

title: IBM fired at least 1,00,000 in recent years to appear 'cool' and 'trendy', lawsuit shows
summary: A former vice president of human resources for IBM testified in an age discrimination lawsuit that the company fired between 50,000 to 100,000 employees in recent years to appear "cool" and "trendy" to millennials, similar to Amazon and Google. This strategy involved targeting older workers through rolling layoffs to "correct" its seniority mix. IBM has faced several lawsuits regarding age discrimination and has seen a 19% reduction in its global workforce since 2013, coinciding with nearly seven years of shrinking revenue.

title: How the Accused Capital One Hacker Stole Reams of Data From the Cloud
summary: Paige Thompson, a former Amazon.com cloud-computing employee, is accused of stealing 106 million Capital One Financial records by exploiting a known cloud vulnerability. This incident highlights ongoing concerns among cybersecurity professionals about the security of cloud-based data. The alleged data theft represents one of the largest bank-data heists in history.

title: U.S. Senator Sends Letter to Amazon CEO on Capital One Hack
summary: Senator Ron Wyden has sent a letter to Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos requesting details about the security of Amazon's cloud service, which was implicated in the recent Capital One hack. The hack involved the theft of 106 million credit-card records stored on Amazon's cloud. This inquiry comes amidst one of the largest bank-data thefts ever recorded.

title: Murphy USA's Loyalty Program Converts 2M Customers to Full Membership
summary: Murphy USA's new loyalty program, Murphy Drive Rewards (MDR), has successfully converted 2.2 million customers to full membership since its national launch in March. President and CEO Andrew Clyde highlighted that the program is driving customer traffic and showing encouraging behavioral changes among loyal customers, with 500,000 new participants joining monthly. The company plans to convert the 7 million non-member participants, seeing significant upside in engaging them.

title: Largest US Beauty Retailer Signs Lease with Largest NYC Landlord
summary: SL Green Realty has signed Ulta Beauty Inc. to a 12,040-square-foot retail space at 2 Herald Square, a prime location in New York City. This deal brings the largest U.S. beauty retailer to a highly trafficked area and fully leases the retail portion of the property, which SL Green recapitalized after acquiring its leasehold interest in 2018. The move underscores the importance of brick-and-mortar presence in key urban markets.

title: Capital One data breach: The main takeaway for consumers
summary: The Capital One data breach, affecting over 106 million customers, highlights the critical need for consumers to actively monitor and protect their financial information. Experts advise regular transaction monitoring, varied passwords, security questions, and suspicious activity alerts to prevent personal financial crises. While consumers have a role, companies are ultimately responsible for data protection and implementing robust cybersecurity measures to prevent such breaches.

title: IBM laid off up to 100,000 workers, Austin man's lawsuit claims
summary: An Austin man's lawsuit claims IBM laid off up to 100,000 workers in recent years, alleging age discrimination. Jonathan Langley, a 60-year-old former cloud salesman, contends he was forced out due to his age as IBM sought to rebrand as a "millennial-centric tech company." This lawsuit is one of several accusing IBM of firing older workers, with reports indicating significant reductions in its global workforce targeting older employees.

title: XPO still working to make up for loss of largest customer
summary: XPO Logistics is still working to recover from the loss of its largest customer, believed to be Amazon, which downsized its operations with XPO in Q4 2018. Despite the impact on revenue growth and the postal injection business, XPO is making progress in replacing lost revenue and is optimistic about growth driven by new technology investments like XPO Smart and XPO Connect. The company also faces challenges from a sluggish freight market but anticipates significant profit growth from its tech initiatives.

title: Future Looks Bright For Decline of Retail Store ETF
summary: The article discusses the increasing challenges faced by traditional retailers due to the growth of online shopping, leading to store closures. It highlights how these trends could benefit the ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (NYSEArca: EMTY), which provides short exposure to traditional retailers. EMTY's strong year-to-date performance is noted, reflecting the continued decline in brick-and-mortar retail and the shift towards e-commerce.

title: FedEx terminates ground delivery of Amazon packages in US
summary: FedEx announced it will not renew its ground-delivery contract with Amazon when it expires at the end of August, further cutting ties with the e-commerce giant which is also a competitor in the logistics sector. This decision follows an earlier move where FedEx's Express unit stopped flying Amazon's packages in the U.S. FedEx states this move aligns with its strategy to focus on the broader e-commerce market, while Amazon continues to build its own extensive logistics network.

title: Mercer Mega Block sale could haul in $143.5 million for city of Seattle
summary: The city of Seattle is negotiating the sale of the Mercer Mega Block for $143.5 million to Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. The deal, if approved, would allocate nearly $80 million to affordable housing efforts, $5 million to homelessness services, and $25 million to transportation projects. The developer plans to build a life sciences campus, a community center, and 175 units of affordable housing on the 3-acre South Lake Union site.

title: FedEx Amazon contract for ground delivery won't be renewed, FedEx says
summary: FedEx announced it will not renew its ground delivery contract with Amazon, effective at the end of August, citing Amazon's growing internal delivery network as a direct competitor. This decision follows a previous termination of their air delivery contract, though FedEx will continue some international Amazon package deliveries. FedEx stated that Amazon constituted only 1.3% of its total revenue in 2018, or approximately $850 million, and that the e-commerce landscape is shifting with increased priority from retailers like Walmart and Target.

title: Altice partners with Devialet for Alexa speaker that can control your TV box
summary: Altice USA has partnered with French audio brand Devialet to launch its first smart speaker, the Altice Amplify. This Alexa-enabled speaker offers hands-free voice control of the Altice One TV platform in addition to standard smart speaker features. The Altice Amplify will be available later this year, priced at $399 for Altice customers and $499 for non-customers.

title: PepsiCo Executive to Become UPS Finance Chief
summary: United Parcel Service Inc. has appointed Brian Newman, a PepsiCo executive, as its new chief financial officer, effective September 16. Newman will succeed Richard Peretz, who is set to retire at the end of the year. This move comes as UPS aims to capitalize on the strained relationship between FedEx and Amazon and reflects a broader management strategy to bring in outside talent for change.

title: Netflix Global Real Estate Grab: How the Streamer Is Expanding From London to Singapore
summary: Netflix is rapidly expanding its physical presence globally through significant investments in studio facilities and high-end office spaces. The company has acquired or leased properties in major cities worldwide, including Toronto, London, Mexico City, New York, Mumbai, Singapore, and Seoul, to support its booming content production and growing employee base. This expansion reflects a strategic move to establish localized hubs for content creation and corporate operations.

title: Residence Inn next to Amazon’s future HQ sells for $99 million
summary: Host Hotels & Resorts has sold The Residence Inn Arlington Pentagon City for US$99.1 million to an LLC registered to Blackstone’s headquarters. The 23-year-old, 299-key extended stay hotel is adjacent to Amazon’s future HQ and underwent renovation in 2012. This sale is part of Host's strategy to divest properties and buy back its own shares, having sold $609 million in hotel properties in 2019 so far.

title: Postmates cleared for robot deliveries in SF — Marble wants in, too
summary: Postmates has received a permit to begin testing its autonomous delivery rover, Serve, in a limited capacity in San Francisco. The permit allows for testing only three robots at a time in specific industrial areas, at low speeds, and with a human escort within 30 feet. Another robot-delivery company, Marble, has also applied for a permit, indicating a growing interest in autonomous delivery despite past regulatory hurdles in the city.

title: Paycom No. 6 on Fortune’s list of fastest-growing companies
summary: Paycom Software Inc., a provider of cloud-based human capital management software, has been ranked No. 6 on Fortune magazine’s 2019 100 Fastest-growing Companies list. The Oklahoma City-based company, which is the only human capital management provider on the list, also saw its CEO, Chad Richison, recognized among Glassdoor's Top 100 CEOs for 2019. Paycom's strong performance was driven by significant revenue growth, a high employee approval rating, and positive business outlook among its staff.

title: Target CEO Brian Cornell sees turnaround as 'still in early innings'
summary: Target CEO Brian Cornell reflects on his five years leading the company's turnaround, comparing it to the 1969 Mets' Cinderella season. He acknowledges the significant progress made, transforming Target from a struggling retailer into one with robust sales growth and rising traffic, despite initial skepticism from Wall Street. Cornell emphasizes a measured, "go slow to go fast" approach, focusing on store remodels, private-label brands, new services, and a more externally focused leadership team while acknowledging ongoing challenges from competitors and economic factors.

title: Big health plans pledge to look beyond shareholders. Critics aren’t so sure
summary: Major health plans, including CVS Health, Anthem, and Cigna, have signed a Business Roundtable statement indicating a shift from prioritizing only shareholders to considering all stakeholders. However, critics and political figures like Sen. Elizabeth Warren remain skeptical, calling for concrete actions. Kaiser Permanente CEO Bernard Tyson declined to sign, stating that as a non-profit, Kaiser does not have shareholders to prioritize.

title: Costco Children's Golf Classic brings in record sum, country star brings down the house
summary: The Friends of Costco Guild's 20th annual Children’s Golf Classic achieved a record sum. The three-day event, starting August 17, included a VIP party, dinner with entertainment, and a golf tournament across nine local courses. The article highlights the success of this long-standing charity event.

title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses shed their own facilities. This trend is leading to increased deals and consolidation among data-center landlords and cloud providers as they seek more capacity. Companies like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. are major drivers of this demand for co-location services.

title: Mystery new Sonos Move could be company’s first portable Bluetooth speaker
summary: Sonos is expected to launch its first portable Bluetooth speaker, named the Move, designed to work both within a home Wi-Fi network and as a standalone Bluetooth device. The speaker will feature Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Apple AirPlay 2, and voice control via Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, along with an Auto Trueplay feature for automatic sound tuning. It will be battery-powered with a charging dock and a USB-C port, marking a significant expansion for Sonos into portable audio.

title: Apple, JPMorgan CEOs Say Companies Must Serve More Than Shareholders
summary: 181 CEOs of major public companies, including Apple, JPMorgan Chase, and Walmart, have declared their companies' purpose extends beyond just shareholders to include all stakeholders like customers, employees, and communities. This new stance, articulated by the Business Roundtable, signifies a shift away from the "shareholder primacy" theory that has guided corporate governance for decades, reflecting growing public and generational expectations for corporate responsibility. The declaration suggests that capitalism, when adjusted, can be a force for broader societal good.

title: Corsair unveils $100 K57 RGB Wireless gaming keyboard with Slipstream tech
summary: Corsair has unveiled its new K57 RGB Wireless gaming keyboard, priced at $100, featuring sub-1ms wireless connectivity via Slipstream tech or Bluetooth 4.2. It boasts 35-hour battery life with RGB LEDs enabled, quiet rubber dome switches with 8-key roll-over, and customizable macro keys, making it a compelling option for gamers. The keyboard also incorporates CAPELLIX LEDs for brighter illumination and less power consumption.

title: Tom Lydon on Varney & Co: Hot Online Retail ETFs
summary: ETF Trends CEO Tom Lydon appeared on Fox Business Network's "Varney & Co." to discuss online retail ETFs, highlighting the decline of big-box retailers and the rise of online sales. He introduced ETFs like ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY) and ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), as well as ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX) for a combined strategy. The article also touches on mixed Q2 earnings for Home Depot and Kohl's, despite the general downturn in traditional retail.

title: NVIDIA and VMware to Accelerate Machine Learning, Data Science and AI Workloads on VMware Cloud on AWS Accelerated by NVIDIA GPUs
summary: NVIDIA and VMware are partnering to offer accelerated GPU services for VMware Cloud on AWS, aimed at enhancing AI, machine learning, and data analytics workflows. This collaboration will provide a highly scalable and secure hybrid cloud platform, enabling enterprises to seamlessly migrate and modernize applications. The service, utilizing NVIDIA T4 GPUs and NVIDIA Virtual Compute Server software, will offer benefits such as seamless portability, elastic AWS infrastructure, and accelerated computing for modern applications.

title: Ubiquiti UniFi Review
summary: This article reviews the Ubiquiti UniFi networking system, highlighting its flexibility and user-friendly management through the UniFi Controller. It details the setup, performance, and build quality of the UniFi Security Gateway (USG), Switch 8 150W, and UniFi nanoHD access point, concluding that it's a powerful solution for those serious about their home network.

title: Arbitrator denies Atlas Air’s pilots bid to negotiate; imposes arbitrated settlement
summary: An arbitrator denied Atlas Air pilots' request to negotiate their next contract, instead imposing an arbitrated settlement, a legal victory for Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings, Inc. The decision means the pilots will not be able to vote on or ratify the contract. The union has vowed to pursue all legal options to avoid an arbitrated contract, while pilots argue they are underpaid and their previous concession promises were not kept.

title: Crowds force Costco to shut 1st China store early on opening day
summary: Costco's first store in China, located in Shanghai, was forced to close early on its opening day due to overwhelming crowds and resulting traffic jams. Videos showed thousands of people in the aisles, and local authorities advised residents to shop during off-peak hours for safety. This event occurred as other Western retailers have struggled to gain market share in China against strong local competition.

title: Red Hat CEO Says Acquisition by IBM Will Help Spur More Open-Source Innovation
summary: Red Hat CEO Jim Whitehurst stated that IBM's acquisition of Red Hat will foster more open-source innovation, emphasizing a collaborative "two cultures working together" approach. The acquisition aims to strengthen IBM's cloud business by enabling customers to use Red Hat's open-source software across various cloud providers, including IBM's own cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. Red Hat's technology helps CIOs run applications both in their own data centers and across third-party cloud services, enhancing flexibility and reducing risk.

title: Crocs Are Cool. Yes, Really.
summary: This article argues that despite divided opinions on their appearance, Crocs are an attractive investment due to their increasing popularity and strong sales performance. The author highlights that Crocs are in vogue, with rising search interest and high rankings among best-selling shoes on Amazon.

title: The age of disloyalty: most Singaporean shoppers open to new brands
summary: A new study reveals that brand loyalty is low among Singaporean shoppers, with 78% willing to consider new brands, especially for groceries and apparel. The Criteo S.A. Why We Buy survey found that consumers value good value and wide product selection over traditional loyalty programs. The study emphasizes that brands need to appeal beyond low prices and loyalty points by focusing on brand values and personalized online ads due to Singapore's high internet connectivity.

title: HPE Takes VMware Cloud Users On Its Synergy Journey To Greenlake
summary: HPE is expanding its GreenLake cloud-like IT consumption model by partnering with VMware to integrate GreenLake and HPE Synergy with VMware Cloud Foundation. This collaboration allows joint customers to run VMware Cloud Foundation as a service on GreenLake, offering a cloud-like experience with greater flexibility and cost efficiency in their own datacenters. The initiative is part of HPE's ambitious plan to deliver its entire portfolio as a service by 2022, leveraging GreenLake's metering and capacity management capabilities to optimize IT environments.

title: Gartner Identifies Four Emerging Trends That Will Transform How Marketers Run Their Technology Ecosystems
summary: Gartner has identified four emerging trends in its Hype Cycle for Digital Marketing and Advertising 2019 report that are set to transform how marketers manage their technology ecosystems: Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), AI for Marketing, Blockchain for Advertising, and Real-time Marketing. These technologies are expected to have a significant impact on delivering meaningful customer experiences and driving business value. The report details the current state and future implications of each trend, highlighting ongoing challenges and opportunities for marketers.

title: Click, drive, pick up. Target takes drive-up service nationwide
summary: Target is expanding its drive-up service nationwide, allowing customers to order online and pick up purchases at nearly 1,750 stores across all 50 states. This expansion aims to enhance convenience for shoppers, a strategy increasingly adopted by retailers to compete with Amazon. The service typically allows customers to have their orders brought to their cars within two minutes of arrival.

title: WPP forges closer links to big tech with launch of San Francisco campus
summary: WPP is opening a new campus in San Francisco to better serve major tech clients like Google, Facebook, and Amazon, and to foster collaboration between its agencies and tech platforms. This move is part of CEO Mark Read's three-year turnaround plan, aiming to transform WPP into a "creative transformation company" and address declining sales in key markets. The campus, which will house over 1000 people, is expected to be operational in the third quarter of 2021.

title: DOD awards $7.6B Microsoft Office 365 cloud contract to General Dynamics and partners
summary: The U.S. Defense Department has awarded a $7.6 billion, 10-year contract to General Dynamics Corp. subsidiary CSRA LLC, in partnership with Dell Technologies Inc. and Minburn Technology Group LLC, to standardize its email and collaboration workflows on Microsoft's Office 365. This Defense Enterprise Office Solutions (DEOS) program aims to migrate 1.5 million users to Office 365, with an initial focus on moving personnel off the aging Defense Enterprise Email system. The contract also highlights the requirement for Impact Level 6 certification for Secret-level data, which Microsoft is reportedly still obtaining, using its recently authorized Azure cloud regions.

title: BlackRock in Amazon: ‘World’s largest investor in deforestation’
summary: A report by Friends of the Earth US, Amazon Watch, and Profundo labels BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, as the "world's largest investor in deforestation" due to its extensive investments in companies linked to the destruction of forests in Brazil. The report highlights BlackRock's increased holdings in high-risk sectors such as soy, beef, palm oil, rubber, timber, and pulp/paper, despite the company's commitment to engaging with firms on sustainability. Critics argue that BlackRock's passive investment strategies and reliance on the ESG industry's data fail to adequately address deforestation risks.
